pages.title: How to Create a Monster
pages.content:
The Composition Pipeline

A monster in 1547 is assembled by stacking ChangeSets onto a base actor in a fixed order. Each step builds on the previous, layering identity, tactics, and signature behavior.

  1. Type — pick a base family from the TypeDropdown on the actor (HiddenFolk, Spirit, Beast, Undead, TheUnseen, Unnatural, Construct, Colossal, Zone, People). Setting this auto-applies the matching Base ChangeSet, giving the monster its baseline stats, traits, signature powers, and natural weapons (where appropriate).
  2. Role — its combat function (e.g. Pack Hunter, Brute, Ambusher, Caster).
  3. Domain — its sphere of influence (Forest, Crossroads, Crypt, etc.).
  4. Loadout — its body plan, gear, or weapon set (Quadruped, Tailed, Constrictor, Winged, Colossal Predator, Tusks+Horn).
  5. Motivation — what drives it (Territorial, Cursed, Hungry, Bound).
  6. Quirks — flavor traits and tactical edges (no hard cap; pick as many as fit).
  7. Boosts — power-level scaling, rolled on the Standard Boost Table (see the Boost Roll Table reference chapter). Each boost adds +1 to a stat, an extra die to a natural weapon, or a granted maneuver.

Two ways to build

1. The Monster Wizard (easiest)

Click the Monster Wizard button at the top of the Actor Directory. Walk through eight steps:

  1. Name & Type — required.
  2. Role — pick one or skip.
  3. Domain — pick one or skip.
  4. Loadout — pick one or skip.
  5. Motivation — pick one or skip.
  6. Quirks — check any number (or none).
  7. Review & Create — confirm picks. Click Create Actor — the actor is built, ChangeSets attached, Base auto-applied.
  8. Boosts (optional) — click Roll Boost as many times as you want. Each roll resolves immediately with an Apply/Skip prompt. Click Done when satisfied; the actor sheet opens.

2. Manual composition

If you want full control:

  1. Create a new actor (template type). Set TypeDropdown — the Base auto-applies.
  2. Drag desired ChangeSets onto the actor sheet from the Change Sets compendium. Order doesn't strictly matter, but the canonical pipeline order (Role → Domain → Loadout → Motivation → Quirk) makes monsters easier to read.
  3. Use the Boost button on the actor sheet to roll boosts as needed. Boosts stack — three Strength boosts give +3 Strength mod.

Tier and balance

The monster's tier is the count of Boost ChangeSets attached. Use it as a rough power yardstick when matching monsters to encounters. The tier badge at the top of the actor sheet shows the count plus a summary (e.g. Strength ×2 · Dex · Sta).

Editing afterward

You can drop more ChangeSets on a finished monster, swap one out, or boost again at any time — the composition pipeline reapplies and the actor refreshes.
